historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Triptans

starting.description: Clinical observations that intravenous serotonin could relieve migraine, despite substantial adverse effects, motivated a search for the receptor responsible for its beneficial action and a more selective agonist. Clinical and animal observations involving methysergide also helped focus the team's receptor hypothesis.

inspiration.description: The starting clues included a reported clinical effect of the endogenous signaling molecule serotonin, clinical responses to methysergide, and methysergide's observed action in an animal carotid circulation. Researchers sought to separate beneficial from unwanted serotonin effects through receptor selectivity.

steps.description: Reports of migraine relief following intravenous serotonin, tempered by problematic side effects, gave the Glaxo team a clinical effect to develop.
Lance's clinical observations and Saxena's animal work on methysergide, followed by the team's own experiments, focused attention on a potentially distinct serotonin receptor in cranial circulation.
The team sought the relevant serotonin receptor and designed selective agonists; the research led to sumatriptan.
An early open clinical study reported responses to intravenous GR43175; Humphrey later attributed the development of similar triptans to sumatriptan's clinical success.

design.description: Deliberate design created a serotonin-related molecule with a different receptor-selectivity profile, aiming to retain the desired effect while reducing other serotonin effects.

circumstances.description: The Glaxo team's receptor search and development of selective agonists were deliberate; this does not characterize the circumstances of the earlier clinical observation.

limits: The record addresses the sumatriptan founding program and class establishment; it does not reconstruct or presume the detailed research lineage of every later triptan.
The 1960 report did not establish a peripheral mechanism of relief; the later vascular explanation is a historical development hypothesis, not a conclusion established by that report.
gaps: The 1988 Glaxo GR43175 pharmacology report was read only as an abstract because full-text access attempts were blocked; the 1988 clinical study was also read as an abstract only.
The original Lance methysergide comparison and Saxena animal experiment underlying Humphrey's account were not independently reopened; their causal role is reported from his retrospective.
Detailed chemical intermediate sequence and each subsequent analogue's research history were not reconstructed; no priority claim is made for the 1988 clinical report.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Migraine relief with intravenous serotonin, accompanied by adverse effects, motivated selective agonist development.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: A deliberate human intervention, not noninterventional epidemiology or an incidental side-effect discovery.
